===== ROLE =====
Act as a senior product designer, frontend architect, interaction designer, data-visualization designer, and UX researcher working together on Bloom.
Redesign the existing Bloom Cycle route as a premium React experience, not as a cosmetic refresh.
Study the supplied Cycle screenshots and the supplied generated reference image before changing the implementation.
Use the generated reference as a visual benchmark for hierarchy, density, rhythm, typography, visualization quality, and premium feeling.
Do not copy the Profile page structure.
Do not turn Cycle into another editorial profile page.
Do not solve the redesign by merely changing colors, borders, shadows, or font sizes.
Preserve existing working data, calculations, routes, persistence, and privacy behavior.
Inspect the current React architecture before editing it.
Reuse correct existing components and data contracts where practical.
Only use mock data for clearly identified development or empty-state examples.
Never fabricate personal health data.
Never present estimated information as logged information.
Make uncertainty explicit whenever historical data is insufficient.
Build the page around the idea that Bloom understands a user's current cycle and helps them understand what comes next.
===== VISUAL DIRECTION =====
Create a deep near-black navy background with subtle tonal layering.
Use Bloom's restrained lavender-blue interaction accent.
Use soft pink, green, gold, and violet as cycle-phase series colors.
Keep saturation controlled and premium.
Use large editorial serif typography for major contextual headings.
Use clean sans-serif typography for controls, metrics, and metadata.
Use compact uppercase labels sparingly for technical context.
Use thin low-contrast borders instead of heavy outlines.
Use rounded cards consistently but do not put every piece of content inside a card.
Use surface contrast to create depth.
Use shadows very sparingly.
Do not make the interface look cyberpunk or neon.
Do not add random decorative gradients, blobs, stars, or glows.
Use visual decoration only when it reinforces the cycle concept or hierarchy.
Keep whitespace intentional rather than excessive.
Make the page feel substantially more sophisticated than the current screenshots.
===== HERO =====
Build a dedicated Cycle Intelligence hero.
Show the current cycle day prominently.
Show the current phase next to the cycle day.
Add a concise sentence explaining the current state.
Place a large interactive circular cycle visualization as the visual anchor.
Represent menstrual, follicular, ovulation, and luteal phases as proportional arcs.
Calculate arc proportions from real cycle data.
Place the current day marker on the correct position around the wheel.
Make the current marker visually distinct without using a huge glow.
Put the cycle day and total cycle length in the center of the wheel.
Show a compact edit-cycle action near the wheel.
Provide a text alternative for the visualization.
Allow phase segments to be selected.
Show contextual information when a phase is selected.
Do not require hover to understand the visualization.
Make the visualization keyboard accessible.
Distinguish logged stretches from estimated stretches.
Use softer visual treatment for estimates.
===== AT A GLANCE =====
Create an At a Glance intelligence area beside the cycle wheel on desktop.
Show next-period information when available.
Show ovulation information only when supported by the application's data model.
Show fertile-window information only when appropriate.
Show the personal average cycle length when enough completed cycles exist.
Show data confidence or data sufficiency when it materially affects interpretation.
Use compact visual markers instead of four identical generic statistic cards.
Make each item interactive when deeper information exists.
Provide a View all insights action.
Keep the intelligence rail subordinate to the hero.
===== TIMELINE =====
Create a premium Next 7 days timeline below the hero.
Represent each day as a point on a continuous visual path.
Show date, phase, fertility state, and confidence when appropriate.
Highlight today clearly.
Use distinct visual treatment for logged and estimated days.
Make each day selectable.
Show selected-day details inline or in a compact panel.
Do not force users into a modal for simple date information.
Allow the selected date to open the advanced log.
Make the timeline locally scrollable on small screens when necessary.
Never create page-level horizontal scrolling.
===== INSIGHTS =====
Create a Today's Insight module based on actual available signals.
Do not generate generic AI copy just to fill the section.
Use cycle phase, mood, energy, sleep, symptoms, and other existing signals only when available.
Explain which signals contributed to an insight.
Use cautious language for correlations.
Never claim medical causation from tracking data.
Provide a Why this action for transparency.
Allow useful insights to be dismissed when appropriate.
Use warm, concise, human writing.
Create a meaningful insufficient-data state.
===== QUICK LOG =====
Create a compact Quick Log module near the hero.
Provide fast access to common cycle logging actions.
Support flow when the existing application supports it.
Support symptoms when the existing application supports it.
Support mood when the existing application supports it.
Support energy when the existing application supports it.
Support sleep when the existing application supports it.
Support basal temperature when the existing application supports it.
Support cervical mucus or discharge when the existing application supports it.
Support notes when the existing application supports it.
Open lightweight focused controls rather than forcing navigation through multiple pages.
Update the Cycle page immediately after a successful log.
Do not turn Quick Log into a giant form.
===== HISTORY =====
Create a Cycle History visualization using actual completed cycle records.
Show average cycle length.
Show cycle-length range when enough history exists.
Show average period length when enough history exists.
Show luteal information only when it can be calculated reliably.
Make historical chart marks interactive.
Selecting a cycle should reveal its dates and summary.
Do not render fabricated history.
Create an honest empty state when history is insufficient.
Explain how more completed cycles improve personal averages.
Keep generalized baseline information visually distinct from personal history.
===== PATTERNS =====
Create a Your Patterns section that translates raw logs into understandable observations.
Show recurring cycle-day patterns when enough data exists.
Show recurring period-length patterns when enough data exists.
Show recurring symptom timing when enough data exists.
Show recurring energy or mood relationships when enough data exists.
Show the number of observations supporting a pattern.
Prefer phrases such as seen in 4 of 5 cycles over false precision.
Separate observation from interpretation.
Never present a pattern as a diagnosis.
Make each pattern expandable for more detail.
===== CORRELATIONS =====
Create a Lifestyle Correlation section using real logged data.
Allow examples such as sleep versus cycle length when enough data exists.
Allow energy versus phase when enough data exists.
Allow mood versus phase when enough data exists.
Allow symptom frequency versus phase when enough data exists.
Label these relationships as observations rather than causes.
Show sample size.
Do not render meaningless charts with too few observations.
Provide graceful insufficient-data states.
Explain the calculation method through a secondary disclosure.
===== PHASES =====
Create a visually refined Cycle Phases education section.
Give menstrual, follicular, ovulation, and luteal phases distinct restrained visual identities.
Use subtle abstract SVG artwork or texture where it improves comprehension.
Explain what each phase generally represents.
Show typical day ranges only when meaningful.
Use plain language.
Allow deeper explanations through expandable content.
State clearly that individual cycles vary.
Do not turn educational material into medical advice.
===== CALENDAR =====
Redesign the calendar as an intelligence tool rather than a large empty grid.
Show the current month clearly.
Provide previous, next, and Today controls.
Represent logged period days distinctly.
Represent estimated period days distinctly.
Represent fertile estimates distinctly.
Represent estimated ovulation distinctly.
Represent today distinctly.
Make dates selectable.
Show selected-date cycle context without requiring a separate page.
Keep the calendar visually lighter than the hero.
Do not make every calendar cell look like a large card.
Make the calendar responsive.
===== ADVANCED LOG =====
Preserve the existing advanced logging functionality.
Redesign the form to belong visually to the new Cycle intelligence system.
Group related fields logically.
Use a two-column layout on desktop where it improves scanning.
Use one column on mobile.
Keep native accessible controls.
Preserve existing fields supported by the application.
Keep sensitive information private and visually restrained.
Show saved state clearly.
Update predictions after relevant new data is entered.
===== AI ASSISTANT =====
Add a floating Bloom AI assistant to the Cycle page.
Make it feel native to Bloom rather than a generic customer-support chatbot.
Use a refined floating action button in the lower corner.
Use subtle animation only when a genuinely useful new insight exists.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Open a compact assistant panel from the button.
Let the assistant use the current cycle context only when the user has permitted that context.
Let it reference actual available logs.
Make the assistant explain why a suggestion was produced.
Provide contextual starter prompts.
Examples include What should I pay attention to today, Why am I seeing this pattern, and Help me prepare for the next few days.
Do not use generic chatbot prompts unrelated to Cycle.
Allow assistant actions to open the relevant log or insight.
Do not invent values.
Do not claim medical certainty.
Make the assistant useful even when almost no history exists.
===== REACT =====
Implement the redesign as real reusable React components.
Separate data calculations from visual components.
Create reusable components for the cycle wheel, insight rail, timeline, quick log, history chart, pattern cards, correlation charts, phase cards, calendar, and AI assistant.
Follow the project's existing naming and folder conventions.
Reuse existing design tokens when available.
Use CSS variables for new design tokens when needed.
Use semantic HTML.
Use real buttons and links for actions.
Use responsive SVG for custom visualizations.
Give every SVG a viewBox.
Do not hardcode visualization geometry that breaks at different sizes.
Keep derived values derived from source data.
Prevent unnecessary rerenders of expensive visualizations.
Do not rewrite the whole application unnecessarily.
===== DATA =====
Audit every number shown on the page.
Never show a predicted value as logged.
Never show a personal average without enough personal observations.
Never show a percentage with a meaningless denominator.
Never label incomplete data as healthy or normal.
Never imply that a predicted ovulation date is guaranteed.
Handle zero completed cycles.
Handle one incomplete cycle.
Handle several completed cycles.
Handle irregular cycles.
Handle missing optional fields.
Handle future dates safely.
Treat date-only values as calendar dates.
Use consistent date calculations across time zones.
===== EMPTY STATES =====
Design every empty state intentionally.
When there are no completed cycles, explain that personal averages will appear as data accumulates.
When there are no logs today, suggest one small useful action.
When there is insufficient data for correlations, explain what additional data would unlock them.
When there are no symptoms, do not imply that the user has forgotten something.
When predictions are unavailable, explain why.
Use calm encouraging copy.
Do not make empty states look broken.
===== RESPONSIVE =====
Support wide desktop layouts.
Support laptop layouts.
Support tablets.
Support mobile widths down to approximately 320 CSS pixels.
Never introduce page-level horizontal scrolling.
Stack the hero intelligently on mobile.
Move At a Glance below the wheel on narrow layouts.
Make the seven-day timeline touch friendly.
Make Quick Log targets large enough to tap comfortably.
Make charts responsive.
Let long text wrap instead of clipping.
Use min-width zero in flexible grid children.
===== POLISH =====
Perform a dedicated visual polish pass after functionality is complete.
Align major sections to a consistent content grid.
Use consistent card radii.
Use consistent border opacity.
Use consistent icon sizes.
Use consistent section spacing.
Remove accidental empty space.
Remove duplicate information.
Strengthen hierarchy around important metrics.
Reduce contrast for secondary metadata.
Do not let decorative elements compete with data.
Make the page feel designed rather than assembled.
Make the page clearly different from Profile.
Make the page feel like Bloom's flagship Cycle experience.
===== IMAGE_GENERATION =====
Before finalizing the implementation, generate a high-fidelity desktop mockup inspired by the supplied reference image.
Use the reference image to match the overall composition, hierarchy, proportions, and visual language.
Generate a second desktop variation with an alternative intelligence layout.
Generate a mobile mockup showing the responsive hierarchy.
Generate an open-state mockup showing the Bloom AI assistant.
Generate these images before the final visual polish pass when the environment supports image generation.
Use the generated mockups as implementation references rather than production assets.
Compare the browser implementation against the generated mockups.
Correct major spacing, hierarchy, chart density, and proportion differences discovered during comparison.
Do not blindly introduce elements from generated images that the existing data model cannot support.
===== QA =====
Run TypeScript checking.
Run linting.
Run the production build.
Open the Cycle route in a real browser.
Test with zero data.
Test with one cycle.
Test with multiple completed cycles.
Test with irregular cycles.
Test period logging.
Test advanced log editing.
Test calendar navigation.
Test timeline selection.
Test insight interaction.
Test the AI assistant.
Test mobile responsiveness.
Test keyboard navigation.
Test reduced motion.
Confirm there are no console errors.
Confirm there are no broken imports.
Confirm there are no fabricated production values.
===== FINAL STANDARD =====
Do not stop after redesigning the hero.
Do not stop after adding a cycle wheel.
Complete the full page architecture.
Complete every relevant interaction.
Complete empty states.
Complete loading states.
Complete error states.
Complete responsive behavior.
Complete accessibility behavior.
Complete visual polish.
Compare the final browser result with the supplied reference image.
Iterate until the Cycle page looks like a premium dedicated product rather than a generic tracker.
Make the page more useful as the user's data history grows.
Make the page honest and useful when data is sparse.
Make every visual element communicate something meaningful.
Make the final experience feel calm, intelligent, premium, and unmistakably Bloom.
